items.title: Reconcile REPORT.md's Known Issues and hand-off with this run's fixes
items.acceptance: REPORT.md's Known Issues table and hand-off section state the resolved/bounded status of KI-1, KI-6 and KI-7 and the newly machine-checked status of KI-5, with no remaining claim that any of them is still open, unswept, or documented in prose only.
items.notes:
Not a test item. Runs LAST by deps - once T-101..T-104 land, REPORT's current statements become false, which is the exact doc-truth failure mode SPEC must-have 6 and L-026 warn about. Also record KI-3 as resolved (remote + gh auth verified at kickoff).

HANDOFF FROM T-101 (cycle 4), three things this item now owns:
(1) RESOLVED-STATUS CONVENTION. KI-1 and KI-6 are both in state.json resolved_issues, but REPORT.md's Known Issues table still LISTS them as rows (KI-1's row now carries the completed finding at severity low; KI-6's row still reads as open). T-101 was explicitly forbidden from inventing a convention in the severity column - that column must stay severities only. THIS item decides the convention (a separate status column, a struck row, a Resolved section - conductor's call) and applies it to KI-1, KI-3, KI-6, and KI-7 once bounded. Do NOT put status strings in the severity column.
(2) The table header still says 'Known issues (7)'. If rows move out, the count moves with them.
(3) RESIDUAL flagged by the T-101 gate, not fixed there because it was outside that item's acceptance: README.md line ~27 opens 'Most terminal moon phase tools compute the phase with a naive synodic-month modulo, which drifts by hours to days.' The sweep substantiates that for ONE package (the nearest), not for 'most', and 'hours to days' is an unsourced pre-existing magnitude. The standing no-unsourced-numbers rule says a quantity may appear only in the frame the repo already computes it in. Either source it, scope it to the one package the sweep actually examined, or drop the magnitude.

DEP UPDATE cycle 8: T-103b is now done. T-108's remaining open dep is T-109.

DEP UPDATE cycle 9: T-109 is now done. ALL DEPS CLOSED - T-108 is unblocked and is the highest-value item left on the backlog.
CYCLE-10 GATE: FAILED at haiku, attempt 1, whole diff reverted (evidence:
.swarm/runs/cycle-010-verify-T-108.txt). Four of six checks passed; two failed, both
inside the run's doc-truth premise.

WHAT PASSED and must be REPRODUCED, not rediscovered — attempt 1 got these right:
 - The status-column table renders correctly and the severity column stayed severities.
 - KI-6's row: the builder read src/astro.js and correctly wrote TypeError (astro.js:358).
 - KI-7's row: domain sourced to the PHASE_ILLUMINATION_CONSISTENCY_DOMAIN constant.
 - `# 102 tests` -> `# 106 tests` in the How-to-run block.
 - Line 3 and line 5 (the original run's historical header) correctly left untouched.

FAILURE 1 — false quantity. Attempt 1 wrote "all 8 commits have been pushed" (KI-3 row)
and "Eight commits have been pushed" (hand-off item 4). `git rev-list --count HEAD` = 24.
The figure was carried out of line 5, where "8 commits" truly records the ORIGINAL run,
and restated in the present tense as a total covering the repo now. "all 8" asserts a
complete inventory, so a reader concludes 16 commits do not exist. The retry must not
state a commit total at all unless it counts one at write time; the honest sentence needs
no number. Hand-off item 4's bold lead-in "**Push it somewhere.**" is an instruction to a
human to do something already done and must go with it.

FAILURE 2 — misattributed magnitude in README (the residual half of this item). Attempt 1
wrote "`lunarphase-js` computes the phase with a naive synodic-month modulo - one that
lands nearly four hours off on the 2000-01-06 new moon". The four-hour figure is computed
in README's own ## Accuracy section for "a mean-formula-only implementation" using THIS
repo's mean-phase formula. lunarphase-js was never run and per the SPEC's Domain rules
uses a different epoch and synodic constant, so the figure is not that package's error.
This is verbatim the T-101 attempt-1 defect the cycle-4 decision recorded. Removing the
"most tools" generalization and then pinning the same borrowed magnitude onto one named
package makes it read MORE authoritative, not less.

FAILURE 2b — self-contradiction. After the rewrite, "It draws the moon from a fixed set of
sprites, which is backwards for the southern hemisphere" binds "It" to lunarphase-js,
while the next paragraph says that package has "hemisphere support that swaps emoji
glyphs". Two sentences apart the file says the package both lacks and has hemisphere
handling. Rebinding the subject from a general class to a named package was the required
fix; carrying the general class's predicate along with it was not.

CYCLE-11 GATE: PASSED at sonnet, attempt 2. Nine conductor-authored checks, nine pass (evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-011-verify-T-108.txt). Both cycle-10 failures are fixed: no commit total is stated anywhere (the obsolete 'Push it somewhere' hand-off item is deleted outright rather than renumbered), and the four-hour figure is attributed to the mean-formula approach in THIS repo's own frame with a cross-ref to ## Accuracy, not to the never-executed lunarphase-js. The self-contradiction is gone: 'takes exactly this route on the math' scopes the naive-route claim so the file no longer says one package both lacks and has hemisphere handling. Convention chosen: a separate status column plus a new ## Resolved issues table; the severity column stayed severities only. Two residuals filed rather than conductor-patched (T-114, T-115) and T-110 widened - see those items.

items.title: Landing T-109 made test/render.test.js's round-limb comment false
items.acceptance: The doc comment governing UNDOCUMENTED_DISC_GLYPHS in test/render.test.js no longer claims the README's width caveat 'never mentions' U+25D6/U+25D7, and describes the actual post-T-109 state: the README names them and explicitly declines to classify their East Asian Width, so they remain outside the documented Neutral/Ambiguous partition the test checks. The assertion itself and UNDOCUMENTED_DISC_GLYPHS' contents must not change - only the prose that describes why they are held apart.
items.notes:
FOUND BY THE CYCLE-9 GATE, and unusual in that this cycle CREATED it rather than uncovering it. test/render.test.js:586-588 reads 'The README's width caveat never mentions them: it is scoped to the Block Element shade ramp and does not claim completeness over every glyph the disc can emit.' As of cycle 9 the README does mention them. The assertion still passes and the test still tells the truth about what is COVERED; it is the explanatory prose that has gone stale.
Filed rather than conductor-patched (cycle 7/8 precedent) and rather than folded into T-109, whose write scope was README.md alone - letting a docs builder reach into the test suite is the opposite of the discipline this run enforces.
Priority 4, ahead of the remaining test items: a live falsehood introduced by this run outranks a test that has been missing since v0.1.0.
WAVE NOTE: overlaps T-113 in test/render.test.js. The two must never share a wave.

items.title: Test package-manifest integrity: bin path, main field, zero deps, files list
items.acceptance: A test confirms package.json's bin.moon path resolves to the same file the CLI suites spawn, its main field resolves to an existing module, it declares no dependencies and no devDependencies, and its files allowlist matches what the package actually ships.
items.notes:
PLAN grep (conductor-verified): zero hits for package.json|require.resolve|dependencies across test/. REPORT.md lists 'zero runtime dependencies' as a VERIFIED claim that no test has ever checked. NOTE: this item READS package.json but must not MODIFY it - manifests are excluded from builder write scope.
DONE cycle 16. Gate: 8/8 package.json mutants killed + ['.'] negative control held (mutate-T-105.py); anti-vacuity floor shown to do independent work (vacuity-T-105.py: neutering the require regex fails via the floor, neutering it with the floor removed passes vacuously); 2/2 cross-file coupling mutants killed after a re-dispatch, both SURVIVED the first draft (xfile-T-105.py); 5/5 extraction breakages fail loudly (extract-T-105.py). 113/113 suite green on branch and on main.

items.title: Test the next-full-moon date label's year-boundary branch
items.acceptance: A test drives the CLI with a clock positioned so the next full moon falls in a later calendar year than the current date and confirms the printed date includes that year; a same-year case confirms the year suffix stays omitted.
items.notes:
PLAN grep (conductor-verified): getFullYear appears exactly once in the repo, at bin/moon.js:61 - the ternary that appends or omits the year. No test references it in either direction; the one date-formatting regression pins day-padding at a fixed 2026-01-01 clock that never crosses a year boundary.
CLOSED cycle 14. Conductor gate: both clock instants re-derived independently from src/astro.js (2025-12-30 -> 2026-01-03, cross-year; 2026-06-01 -> 2026-06-29, same-year), then four mutants of the bin/moon.js year ternary (always-append, never-append, flipped-comparison, prints-now-year) were each killed. M1 was caught only by the same-year test and M2/M4 only by the cross-year test, so the two branches are pinned independently rather than by one test doing both jobs.

items.title: Test that successful CLI invocations write nothing to stderr
items.acceptance: A test confirms every successful invocation mode (default, --compact, --block, --json, --help) produces empty stderr, closing the gap between REPORT.md's 'nothing on stderr on success' VERIFIED claim and a suite that never captures stderr on a passing run.
items.notes:
PLAN grep (conductor-verified): 'stderr' appears in test/ only inside the single --bogus exit-2 test (cli.test.js:107-112). L-010: capture the exit status directly, never through a pipe - use spawnSync and read .status/.stderr, do not shell-pipe.
DONE cycle 18. Gate proved the acceptance's real claim by mutation, not by test count: 6 of 7 stderr mutants pass the PRE-MERGE suite and die against the merged one, and M1-M5 are per-mode, so all five named modes are individually covered. Honest residual recorded in cycle-018-verify-T-107.txt: M6 shows the exit-status half of the assertion was already covered pre-merge (execFileSync throws on non-zero), so only the stderr half is new surface.

items.title: The KI-7 domain doc comment glosses a half-open interval as an inclusive year range
items.acceptance: All THREE places that describe the KI-7 supported domain agree with the half-open interval the constant actually defines - endMs is Date.UTC(3000,0,1) EXCLUSIVE, and test/astro.test.js's loop runs i=0..3999 so its largest sample is strictly below it, meaning calendar year 3000 is NOT covered: (1) src/astro.js's PHASE_ILLUMINATION_CONSISTENCY_DOMAIN doc comment, which currently glosses it as 'calendar years 1000 through 3000' one line above stating the interval correctly; (2) README.md's ## Accuracy paragraph, 'Over years **1000-3000**'; (3) REPORT.md's KI-7 row, 'calendar years 1000-3000'. The constant, the test, and the sample count must not change - only the prose that describes the interval.
items.notes:
FOUND BY THE T-103b GATE at cycle 7, in the module rather than in the item under test. The comment reads 'calendar years 1000 through 3000 (i.e. [Date.UTC(1000,0,1), Date.UTC(3000,0,1)))'. The bracket notation is correct and self-documenting; the prose gloss before it is off by one calendar year at the top end. Low value - the interval notation sits immediately beside the gloss, so a careful reader is not actually misled - but it propagates: T-103b is required to match the module, so the module's imprecision would be copied into README by construction. Fix the module and the README inherits the correct frame.
DELIBERATELY NOT bundled into T-103b: that item's acceptance is 'the domain figures must match the module constant exactly', and letting a docs builder silently re-scope the module's own claim is the opposite of the discipline this run is enforcing.
SCOPE WIDENED cycle 11. T-108 sourced REPORT.md's new KI-7 row to the constant as briefed, and thereby propagated the constant's own inclusive-sounding gloss into a third file. The cycle-11 gate ruled this a defect of the gloss, not of T-108: the builder restated the repo's own declared domain faithfully, and the pre-existing README line says the same thing and passed the cycle-8 gate. Fixing one site and leaving two would leave the repo contradicting itself, so all three move together.
WAVE NOTE: now overlaps T-111, T-113 and T-114 in README.md. No two of those four may share a wave.
DONE cycle 17. Conductor gate: diff scope prose-only across the three named files (constant and test/astro.test.js outside the diff); a conductor-authored discriminator importing the shipping constant and re-reading SAMPLE_COUNT out of the test showed last sample 2999-07-02 < endMs, year 3000 outside the domain, years 1000 and 2999 inside - so the new framing is a fact about both the constant and the test, and the old gloss was false; grep confirms no unqualified inclusive gloss survives in any shipped file; 113/113 green on merged main; CLI smoke clean. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-017-verify-T-110.txt

items.title: README's new KI-7 paragraph uses British 'behaviour'; the repo's prose is US English
items.acceptance: The KI-7 domain paragraph in README.md's ## Accuracy section spells it 'behavior', matching src/astro.js's 'Behavior outside this domain is UNSPECIFIED'. One word, no other change to the paragraph.
items.notes: RESIDUAL FOUND AT THE CYCLE-8 GATE, filed rather than conductor-patched - same handling as T-110 at cycle 7. Measured, not asserted: across HEAD's README.md + src/astro.js + test/astro.test.js the token 'behavior' appears 1x (src/astro.js, KI-7 doc comment) and 'behaviour' 0x; the cycle-8 README addition introduces the first British spelling in the repo. NOT a T-103b acceptance failure - acceptance covers the domain figures, the consequence, and the sampled-test attribution, all of which passed - and failing the run's last must-have over one letter would be gate inflation of exactly the kind cycle 7 warned against when it refused to argue wording as taste. Deliberately NOT fixed by the conductor: cycle 7 established that a conductor editing the artifact leaves nothing independent checking the conductor's own wording, and that rule does not get suspended because the edit is one character.

items.title: 'Fully lit outer cell' understates when the disc draws a round limb
items.acceptance: The three places that describe when ROUND_LIMB is drawn agree with the branch in src/render.js lineArt(), which selects it when the outer cell's lit fraction is >= 0.88 - not only when the cell is fully lit. No threshold figure may be introduced unless it is the constant the source actually uses. Prose only: the 0.88 branch, the glyph set, and every assertion must be left exactly as they are. ALSO (folded in at cycle 12, since this item must edit the same comment block): the same comment's phrase "the README names them and explicitly declines to establish their East Asian Width class" must be narrowed to what README.md:216 actually says — "This repo has not established their East Asian Width class". "Declines to establish" attributes a deliberate refusal the README never states; "has not established" is the fact it does state.
items.notes:
FOUND BY THE CYCLE-9 GATE's truth check, which drove renderLine over 1602 states and then read the governing branch out of source rather than from memory: `else if (cover < 0.88) out += HALF[sunward]; else out += ROUND_LIMB[...]`. So a cell that is 88% lit already draws a round limb.
The claim is TRUE but INCOMPLETE - a fully lit cell does draw one - which is why it did not fail T-109. It also originated in T-109's OWN acceptance text, which the conductor wrote at cycle 5 by lifting src/render.js:63-64's 'Only the fully lit case is positional'; failing a builder for reproducing the item's own words would be gate inflation.
SAME DEFECT FAMILY AS T-110: a module doc-comment gloss slightly wider than the code, which then propagates by construction into every doc that quotes the module. Third instance this run. If a fourth appears, the pattern is worth a playbook lesson rather than another one-off item.
Sites: src/render.js:63-64 (origin), test/render.test.js:585, README.md's new round-limb paragraph. Depends on T-112 to avoid two items editing the same comment block; low value, so it is fine if it never gets built.
SCOPE WIDENED cycle 12 (one phrase, same comment block, no new files). The cycle-12 gate passed T-112 but recorded a residual: the replacement prose says the README "explicitly declines to establish" the EAW class where README.md:216 says it "has not established" it. That gloss came verbatim from T-112's OWN acceptance text, which the conductor wrote at cycle 11 — the cycle-9 precedent (failing a builder for reproducing the item's own words is gate inflation) applies, so T-112 passed. Folded here rather than filed as a sixth one-off row: this item already has to rewrite that exact comment for the fully-lit/0.88 defect, and the spec_digest names CHURN as this run's chief risk.
items.evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-019-verify-T-113.txt — prose-only fix at all 3 sites; discriminator: 2924 of 33192 round-limb draws occur at cover<1.0 (min 0.887324), and outer cells with cover>=0.88 number EXACTLY 33192 = the round-limb draws, so the 0.88 wording is precise in both directions; gate C1-C6 all pass, non-vacuous against HEAD; 114/114 green.

items.title: Propagate the KI-1 prior-art finding into README and REPORT
items.acceptance: README's differentiation claim and REPORT's KI-1 row both state the completed prior-art finding verbatim from SPEC.md (nearest npm package lunarphase-js v2.0.3 is a naive mean-synodic modulo with zero periodic corrections and emoji-only 'hemisphere support', not a CLI; astronomia v4.2.0 is a genuine Meeus port deliberately not adopted as a dependency) in place of the old 'never swept / permission-blocked' language.
items.notes:
PLAN grep (conductor-verified): zero hits for lunarphase-js|astronomia|prior-art in README.md; REPORT.md's KI-1 row still reads 'never swept... permission-blocked', which is now stale. The finding is written out in SPEC.md 'Domain rules' - copy it, do not re-derive it. L-026: never hand-edit captured output.

ATTEMPT 1 FAILED THE GATE (cycle 2), reverted. Model escalated haiku->sonnet. Two defects, both must be avoided on the retry:
(1) GATE-FAILER - FABRICATED MAGNITUDE. The README note asserted the naive modulo gives '4-hour phase errors'. Conductor-verified: the string '4-hour' appears NOWHERE in the repo except the line the builder wrote - not in SPEC.md, not in src/astro.js, not in any prior doc. SPEC's prior-art bullet states 'zero periodic correction terms' and never quantifies the error. It is also probably wrong in the understating direction (Meeus ch.49's single largest periodic term for new/full moon is ~0.40720 d ~= 9.8 h, and the terms sum), so it silently WEAKENS our own differentiation claim while being unverifiable. RULE FOR THE RETRY: state the structural fact (zero periodic corrections vs a full Meeus series) and do NOT quantify the error at all unless the number is computed in-repo and shown.
(2) SHOULD-FIX - the retry put the string 'closed' in the REPORT.md Known Issues table's SEVERITY column, whose other values are medium/low. That conflates status with severity and drops KI-1's real severity (state.json: low). Keep severity a severity; if a resolved-status convention is needed, T-108 owns the table reconciliation - coordinate, do not invent a convention unilaterally here.
CONDUCTOR RULING: this escalation to sonnet must SURVIVE the gear-1 docs demotion rule (which would otherwise push docs items sonnet->haiku). The failure mode was fabrication under the cheaper tier; demoting it back would just reproduce the defect.

ATTEMPT 2 PASSED THE GATE (cycle 4) at sonnet; seven conductor-run checks, evidence in .swarm/runs/cycle-004-verify-T-101.txt. Zero magnitudes introduced (verified by extracting every numeric token from the added lines: only 'KI-1', a list ordinal, and the two SPEC-verbatim version strings v2.0.3/v4.2.0). Severity column holds only severities; KI-1's cell corrected medium->low to match state.json. Stale never-swept language gone from BOTH the table row and the hand-off section. 104/104 green. KI-1 resolved.

CORRECTION TO THE CYCLE-2 RECORD: the stated reason above - that '4-hour' appears NOWHERE in the repo - was a too-narrow grep for the hyphenated literal. The figure IS in-repo in words at README.md:156-157, REPORT.md:34 and test/astro.test.js:96. The gate DECISION was still right: it is a single hand-computed datapoint for the 2000-01-06 lunation, and attempt 1 lifted it into a general per-package error claim about a package nobody ran (understating besides - the largest single ch.49 term is ~9.8h and the terms sum). The retry brief carried this correction so the builder would not be licensed by its own grep.

items.title: Fix KI-6: nextFullMoon throws instead of returning an out-of-range Invalid Date
items.acceptance: Calling nextFullMoon() with a valid Date whose resulting full-moon instant falls outside the representable JS Date range throws a TypeError, matching the module's existing throw-on-bad-input behaviour, instead of silently returning an Invalid Date that later surfaces as an uncaught RangeError from --json's toISOString().
items.notes:
CONDUCTOR-REPRODUCED at cycle 1, first-hand:
  nextFullMoon(new Date(8.64e15)) -> Invalid Date   (silent)
  .toISOString()                  -> RangeError: Invalid time value
  nextFullMoon('not a date')      -> TypeError: nextFullMoon expects a valid Date
PLAN grep (conductor-verified): test/astro.test.js has no hits for RangeError|8640000000000000|275760; its two nextFullMoon throw-tests cover bad INPUT only, never the out-of-range OUTPUT path. Do NOT touch the Meeus math - this is a guard clause on the return value.

GATE PASS at cycle 3 (six conductor-run checks; evidence in .swarm/runs/cycle-003-verify-T-102.txt). Guard is 4 lines on the return value; Meeus math byte-identical. 102 -> 104 tests green. Non-vacuity confirmed: against `git show HEAD:src/astro.js` the defect-pinning test FAILS, so it closes a real surface. KI-6 resolved.

items.title: Declare the KI-7 supported date domain in src/astro.js and pin it with a SAMPLED consistency test
items.acceptance: src/astro.js exports a named constant declaring an explicit supported date-range domain for phaseName/illumination consistency, with a doc comment stating WHY the two Meeus series (ch.48 elongation vs ch.49 instant tables) are only guaranteed consistent inside it. test/astro.test.js SAMPLES points across that declared domain (sampling, never an exhaustive sweep) and asserts the phase name band-discriminator holds at every sampled point.
items.notes:
SPLIT FROM T-103 at cycle 6 (see state.json decisions). This slice owns the MODULE + TEST; the README sentence is T-103b, which deps on this one so the quantity enters the docs only after the repo computes it (standing docs frame rule, cycles 2/4).

CONDUCTOR-MEASURED at cycle 1 - use this, it is sharper than the KI-7 text. The right invariant is a DISCRIMINATOR (L-024): the phase name's illumination BAND must contain the reported illumination - crescent < 0.5, gibbous > 0.5, new < 0.10, full > 0.90 (quarters straddle, exempt). Observed contradictions outside the domain:
  new Date(4.0e15)  -> 'waning gibbous'  ill=0.0385   (gibbous but 3.85% lit)
  new Date(-8.0e15) -> 'waning crescent' ill=0.8053   (crescent but 80.5% lit)
Measured clean region: 0 violations in 32,004 sampled states from year -2000 to 6000; first violation ~72,500 years from 1970. Recommend declaring year 1000-3000 as the supported domain - comfortably inside the measured-clean region with margin. SAMPLED, not exhaustive (taste judge, scope-fits-night).

SCOPE FENCE: this item does NOT change any astronomy. No edits to truePhaseJD, elongationDeg, lunationK, the correction tables, or any polynomial. Adding a constant plus a doc comment plus a test is the whole job. The core is verified against Meeus 49.a/49.b and the SPEC non-goal forbids rewriting it.

The DISCRIMINATOR is the point (L-024): assert the phase name band CONTAINS the reported illumination, not that illumination equals a remembered value. Bands: new < 0.10, waxing/waning crescent < 0.5, waxing/waning gibbous > 0.5, full > 0.90; first/last quarter STRADDLE and are exempt.
items.evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-006-verify-T-103a.txt — astronomy byte-identical to HEAD; 106/106 green; 3733/4000 samples assert (all four bands exercised); conductor mutation (widen endMs to year 80000) turns it RED with a diagnosable message, proving it reads the exported constant AND detects real contradictions; independent re-sample at N=9973 and N=50021 on a jittered off-lattice finds 0 violations.

items.title: State the declared KI-7 supported date domain in README, sourced to the shipping test
items.acceptance: README.md states the same supported date domain that src/astro.js declares, names the consequence of leaving it (phaseName and illumination may contradict each other), and attributes the bound to the in-repo sampled test rather than to an unsourced claim. The domain figures must match the module constant exactly.
items.notes:
SPLIT FROM T-103 at cycle 6. Runs AFTER T-103a so the domain is machine-checked before the README asserts it. STANDING DOCS FRAME RULE (cycles 2 and 4): a quantity may appear only in the frame in which the repo already computes it. Here the frame is exactly what T-103a s test samples - a sampled-clean domain - and the README must not widen it into a proof of correctness outside the sample or into a general accuracy claim.

ATTEMPT 1 FAILED THE GATE at cycle 7 (haiku). Reverted with `git checkout -- README.md`; tree returned clean, 106/106 still green. Read this before retrying - the retry brief is written WITH the correction in it so attempt 2 does not re-argue a settled point.

WHAT ATTEMPT 1 GOT RIGHT (keep all of it): scope fence held (README.md only); the domain figures 1000/3000 were copied correctly from src/astro.js:72-73; NO invented magnitudes (every numeral in the added text already existed in HEAD README or src/astro.js); the consequence was named concretely ('phaseName and illumination may contradict each other') rather than hand-waved; 'Outside this domain, behavior is unspecified' is exactly right; the voice matched the surrounding section.

WHY IT FAILED - ONE CLAUSE. It wrote: 'Over years **1000-3000**, `phaseName` and `illumination` are mutually consistent -- confirmed by test/astro.test.js.' The word CONFIRMED, with no sampling hedge anywhere in the added text, states as established a property the repo only sampled. Every other layer of the repo hedges: src/astro.js says 'SAMPLED-clean, not proven ... not a derived error bound'; test/astro.test.js:386 says 'This SAMPLES -- never exhaustively sweeps --'; the test's own name ends in '(sampled)'. The added README sentence was the ONLY place in the repo asserting the consistency unhedged. Measured at the gate: the test checks 4000 points across a 730,485-day domain = one point per ~183 days, 0.548% of the domain's distinct days. 'Confirmed' asserts a property of a continuum from that sample.

THIS IS NOT A STYLE NOTE. Discriminator the gate applied: if the implementation were wrong at some unsampled instant inside 1000-3000, the module doc comment would still be TRUE ('found no contradiction anywhere in the sample') and the README sentence would be FALSE. A docs item whose job is to document a bound must not make a strictly stronger claim than the module it documents.

WHAT ATTEMPT 2 MUST DO: keep the sentence essentially as-is and carry the hedge into it. The bound is what an in-repo test SAMPLED and found no contradiction in - not what it confirmed, proved, guaranteed, validated or verified. Do not pad the paragraph to compensate; this is a one-clause repair, and the gate will re-check scope, figures and magnitudes exactly as before.

RESIDUAL, NOT A DEFECT IN THIS ITEM (do not 'fix' it, do not widen scope to it): the module's own doc comment glosses the half-open interval [Date.UTC(1000,0,1), Date.UTC(3000,0,1)) as 'calendar years 1000 through 3000', so year 3000 itself is outside the domain but reads as inside. Attempt 1 inherited that phrasing verbatim from the module and was NOT failed for it - matching the module constant is this item's acceptance. Logged separately as T-110.

ATTEMPT 2 PASSED THE GATE at cycle 8 (sonnet). Landed text (README.md, appended to ## Accuracy): 'phaseName and illumination come from two different Meeus series, so nothing guarantees they stay in step forever. Over years 1000-3000, test/astro.test.js samples that domain and finds no contradiction between them; outside it, behaviour is unspecified and the two fields may disagree.' The hedge is carried by construction: 'samples ... and finds no contradiction' mirrors src/astro.js's own 'finds no contradiction ... anywhere in the sample', and the only guarantee-word present is NEGATED ('nothing guarantees'), lifted from the module's 'nothing about them guarantees the two stay in step'. Falsifiability discriminator re-run in the direction cycle 7 demanded: if the implementation were wrong at an unsampled instant inside 1000-3000, the README sentence stays TRUE (the sample still finds none) exactly as the module comment does - parity achieved, which is the whole acceptance clause. Scope 5+/0-, README.md only; numerals on added lines = {1000, 3000} and nothing else. Full gate: .swarm/runs/cycle-008-verify-T-103b.txt

items.title: Pin KI-5 with a test that measures the documented disc glyph widths
items.acceptance: A test inspects the exact glyph set renderLine/renderBlock draw for the disc across a representative sweep of phases and confirms it matches the documented East Asian Width partition (U+2591, U+2590 Neutral; U+2592, U+2593, U+2588, U+258C, U+258F, U+2595 Ambiguous), so a future glyph change fails the gate instead of drifting silently from the documented widths.
items.notes:
PLAN grep (conductor-verified): zero hits for east asian|Ambiguous|2591|2592|258C across test/. KI-5's measured widths exist ONLY as prose in README/REPORT. This item PINS the defect; it does NOT fix it - the glyph-set redesign stays deferred by budget decision.

GATE PASS cycle 5. Conductor-authored gate (.swarm/runs/verify-gate-T-104.mjs, written at verification time): independent conductor-side derivation of the disc glyph set reproduced the builder's 10 codepoints EXACTLY, and the pin FAILS under all three glyph mutations (add an undocumented Block Element, drop a documented one, change the round limb) - so it is a real pin, not a tautology. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-005-verify-T-104.txt

items.title: README's KI-5 glyph list omits the round-limb glyphs it actually draws
items.acceptance: README.md's 'Known limitation: terminal glyph width' section accounts for U+25D6 and U+25D7, the round-limb glyphs the disc actually draws for a fully-lit outer cell - either by adding them to the width partition with their correct East Asian Width class, or by explicitly scoping the section's claim to the Block Element shade ramp. No unsourced magnitude may be introduced (standing docs frame rule, cycle 2/4).
items.notes:
FOUND BY THE T-104 BUILD, cycle 5, and independently CONDUCTOR-CONFIRMED by the gate: the disc's observed glyph alphabet is 10 codepoints - the 8 Block Elements the README lists, PLUS U+25D6 and U+25D7 (ROUND_LIMB in src/render.js, drawn for a fully-lit outer cell). The README's width caveat names only the 8. The builder correctly refused to widen the documented table to make its test pass and pinned the two separately in UNDOCUMENTED_DISC_GLYPHS instead, so the test tells the truth about what is and is not covered; this item closes the doc side.
OPEN QUESTION for whoever takes it: this run has NOT established the EAW class of U+25D6/U+25D7 (both are in fact Ambiguous per Unicode, but that is not machine-checked here and must not be asserted from memory - no EAW table may ship, the zero-dep non-goal forbids it). Scoping the section's claim to the Block Element ramp is the honest S-effort option; classifying the two glyphs requires a source. Do not state a class this repo cannot check.

CLOSED cycle 9, on attempt 2, both attempts inside the same cycle number.
ATTEMPT 1 (session A, died to an API connection error before persisting anything): rewrote the section's opening scope noun to 'The disc's shade ramp and limb glyphs use Unicode Block Elements' and then added a paragraph saying the round limbs are NOT Block Elements. Self-contradictory - ROUND_LIMB is a limb family in src/render.js:69 - so the gate reproduced the contradiction and reverted. Evidence: .swarm/runs/cycle-009-verify-T-109.txt.
ATTEMPT 2 (session B, this record): resolved the OPEN QUESTION above the honest way. It did NOT classify U+25D6/U+25D7 - no EAW class is asserted anywhere in the section - and instead named the covered set precisely ('the shade ramp and its half-block and hairline limb glyphs', mapping 1:1 onto SHADE/HALF/HAIRLINE and structurally excluding ROUND_LIMB), then stated that this repo has not established the round limbs' class and that whether they widen the disc is unknown. 12/12 gate checks, suite 106/106.

items.title: README calls the four-hour figure a 'check'; no executed assertion computes it
items.acceptance: The '## Why this one' paragraph no longer calls the four-hour figure a 'check'. The figure's SUBJECT (the mean-formula-only approach in this repo's own frame), its MAGNITUDE (nearly four hours), and the cross-reference to ## Accuracy must all stay exactly as they are - they are what the cycle-11 gate passed. Only the noun implying an executed assertion changes, to something true of the mechanism that actually exists: MEAN_PHASE_EPOCH in src/astro.js is the k=0 MEAN new moon (JDE 2451550.09766 = 2000-01-06 14:20 TT), the published true instant is 18:14 UTC, README's ## Accuracy section asserts the resulting gap, and test/astro.test.js:97-102 notes in a COMMENT that a mean-formula-only implementation would miss the anchor by ~4h - but no test computes the mean-formula value or asserts the gap.
items.notes:
FOUND BY THE CYCLE-11 GATE (check 9), and like T-112 this run CREATED it rather than uncovering it - the paragraph is the one T-108 attempt 2 rewrote. Passed rather than failed because the defect T-108 was retried against (attributing the figure to the never-executed lunarphase-js) is genuinely fixed; this is one noun overstating a mechanism, with subject and magnitude both correct.
This is the FIFTH instance of the run's signature failure mode: a doc claim slightly wider than what the repo can support. It is a wrap-up distillation candidate, not another one-off - see the cycle-10 journal's note on the fourth instance.
Filed rather than conductor-patched (cycle 7/8/9/10 precedent: a conductor editing the artifact leaves nothing independent checking the conductor's own wording).
WAVE NOTE: overlaps T-110, T-111 and T-113 in README.md. No two may share a wave.

items.title: REPORT's review-fix disclosure says 'this cycle' where the truth is run-wide
items.acceptance: REPORT.md's hand-off states the run-wide truth about the review-fix pass: this run has ONE review-fix pass in its pipeline and it has not been run in ANY cycle, so no part of the document should be read as carrying review coverage. The current sentence ('The run's review-fix pass has not been run this cycle') is true but narrower than the truth and invites the inference that it ran in some other cycle. The disclosure must not be softened or removed - only widened to what is actually the case, and it must say WHY it was deferred (the most premium-heavy work type in the pipeline against an allocator premium allowance that has been 0 throughout).
items.notes:
FOUND BY THE CYCLE-11 GATE (check 9's second residual). Unusual direction for this run: every other doc defect here has been a claim slightly WIDER than the evidence, and this is a disclosure slightly NARROWER than the gap it discloses. Both are the same underlying error - prose that does not track what is actually true - and an under-disclosure in the honesty section is the more corrosive of the two, because that section is exactly where a reader stops checking.
T-108 still improved on the status quo here: before this cycle REPORT.md said nothing at all about review-fix coverage. That is why this is a follow-on item and not a gate failure.
Depends on nothing, but if the review-fix pass DOES run before wrap-up this item is obsolete and should be dropped rather than built.
